thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Stocks Lower After Trump's Apple-production Comments

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Stocks Lower After Trump's Apple-production Comments
text:
By Dow Jones Newswire
Nikkei about flat; indexes in China, Hong Kong, Taiwan slump
Asian stocks were widely lower on Monday, extending last week's selling. President Donald Trump's comments Saturday urging Apple Inc. (AAPL) to move its manufacturing to the U.S. helped pressure Asian tech stocks. The region is home to many of the tech giant's key suppliers, especially in China and Taiwan. Indexes in both were down more than 1%.
Read: Trump urges Apple to move manufacturing to the U.S (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-urges-apple-to-move-manufacturing-to-the-us-2018-09-08).
After an initial 0.3% decline, the Nikkei was last trading up 0.3%, helped by electronics and machinery stocks amid Friday's gains in the dollar. The Nikkei was trying to snap a six-session losing streak. Sony (6758.TO) climbed 0.4% while Fanuc (6954.TO) and Omron (6645.TO) rose 0.9%. Of the 33 Topix subindexes, 20 were up. Banks and insurers were being helped by the end-of-week rise in Treasury yields after the strong U.S. jobs report.
Hong Kong stocks slid along with their mainland counterparts as recent weakness continued. The Hang Seng Index set another 13-month closing low on Friday, and it was last off 1.2%. Macau casinos and Chinese developers remained under pressure amid continued caution regarding U.S.-China trade; the countries' trade gap hit another record in August. Tencent (0700.HK) surrendered early gains after undertaking its first stock buyback in four years.
On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite was down 0.9% while the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite was off close to 2%.
Korea's Kospi rose 0.2% as beaten-down chip companies Samsung (005930.SE) and SK Hynix (000660.SE) climbed amid the Trump-Apple comments. But Taiwan's Taiex sank after those same comments, with Apple suppliers such as Foxconn (2354.TW) dropping over 1% and Largan Precision (3008.TW) sinking over 7%.
Australia's ASX 200 slipped 0.2%, while stocks in New Zealand fell 0.5%, while Singapore's benchmark dropped 0.7%.
